title: Fixed zero-offset power-law mixtures require log-convex counts in equal log-time windows
abstract: We give a necessary count condition for a positive mixture of fixed power-law earthquake rates with zero offsets and one common time origin. Expected counts in three equal log-time windows must be log-convex. We derive an exact conditional Poisson test for excess middle-window counts. In a frozen Ridgecrest sample on days 1-30 at magnitude 2.5 or more, counts are 283, 342, and 306. Log curvature is -0.301 and the one-sided Poisson p value is 0.0170. A three-day residual range is -0.750 to 0.127, and an ml-only test gives p=0.130. The primary result is uncertain. A secondary Puerto Rico sample has counts 187, 692, and 866, curvature -1.084, and a three-day range of -1.469 to -0.723. Later events are a known possible explanation. The test does not cover positive time offsets, later-starting terms, or full triggering models. Poisson independence, short block assumptions, reused catalogs, source selection, and preferred magnitude types limit inference. The package contains the proof, code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, retrieval instructions, and checks.

display.caption: Observed counts in three equal log-time windows, days 1-30, preferred magnitude at least 2.5. A common-origin zero-offset positive power-law mixture requires expected middle counts at or below the log-linear chord. Poisson p values assume independent counts; block uncertainty and magnitude-type checks limit interpretation.
